subject: Operator keystore, onshore egress & private deployment runbook request
messages:
From: Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@clearlinehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Clearline Security <security@clearlinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Data residency and keystore custody questions for pilot

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Clearline's legal and security teams have a few follow-ups before we can scope the pilot:

1) CAIQ / SIG / SOC2: can you provide a redacted CAIQ slice focused on Private Deploy and Key Management, and a SOC2 summary showing control owners and audit scope?

2) Onshore egress guarantee: we need confirmation that API traffic and storage for an EU private deployment will not egress to non-EU regions (including operator telemetry). What mechanisms are in place to enforce region locality and to prove it?

3) Operator keystore access & escrow: please describe how operator/admin access to customer keystores is controlled. Specifically:
  - Are HSMs region-pinned?
  - Do you support split-key escrow?
  - Is operator access time-bound and logged?

4) Runbook / attestation: would you be able to provide a short runbook we can include in our vendor assessment and a signed attestation for residency controls?

Targeting a go/no-go review on Monday, so any artifacts + a 30-min technical call this week would be helpful.

Best,
Alex Dunne
Senior Security Engineer
Clearline Health

---
Note: attaching a sample questionnaire would be great if available.

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency and keystore custody questions for pilot

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. We're assembling a concise packet for you. Attached (see file names below) are the items we can share today:

- Redwood_SOC2_Summary_v1.pdf (scope and control owners, redacted)
- CAIQ_slice_Clearline_v2026-05.xlsx (focused on Private Deploy & Key Mgmt)
- PrivateDeploy_Runbook_v1.2.pdf (operations & connectivity expectations for VPC/private deployments)
- HSM_Partitioning_Summary.txt (high-level partitioning and region scoping)

Quick answers to your specific bullets:
- HSMs are configured by deployment region and we operate with region-scoped key partitions for Private deployments. I will confirm the exact attestation language with infra (cc'ing Marissa and Irene).
- We support split-key escrow models and customer-managed key options; details are in the runbook/attachment.
- Operator access is just-in-time (JIT) with role-based approvals and full audit logging; we'll include a short excerpt for your review.

If that looks reasonable, I've suggested a 30-minute call on Thursday; if you prefer, Marissa (infra) can join to walk through the keystore flow.

Link to the attestation draft: https://drive.redwood.com/s/clearline/attestation-20260514

Irene/Marissa — quick confirmation on HSM region-pinning and whether we can provide a signed attestation stating 'no egress outside EU for customer data and keystore operations' for Clearline?

Thanks,
Mina
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Quick tech confirm for Clearline (HSM / escrow / operator access)

Marissa / Irene —

Please confirm the following for an EU Private Deploy (customer-managed VPC + Redwood Private control plane):

1) HSM partitioning: are HSMs physically or logically region-scoped such that keys for EU deployments cannot be imported/exported to non-EU hardware?
2) Escrow options: we support split-key escrow (Redwood holds a piece under an escrow agreement). Is the standard escrow process documented and can we provide a sample MOU for the customer?
3) Operator access: operator admin sessions are requested via JIT with approval; are session recordings and keystream operations logged to the same retention as SOC2 audit logs?
4) Can we sign a residency attestation that reads: 'Redwood Inference will not transfer customer data or keystore material outside the EU for the contracted private deployment, except as required by law'?

Need short answers so Mina can close the packet and provide the attestation draft to Clearline.

Thanks — Mina

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T11:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Quick tech confirm for Clearline (HSM / escrow / operator access)

Mina —

Short answers below (happy to expand on a call):

1) HSM partitioning: HSM clusters used for Private deployments are logically partitioned per region and we enforce KMS isolate policies at the hypervisor/network layer. Keys provisioned for an EU tenant are tagged and blocked from export to non-EU clusters by policy enforcement. Physical movement requires an infra change request and privileged approval.

2) Escrow: we support split-key escrow. Standard process: customer signs Escrow MOU -> keys are split client-side -> a shard can be stored with Redwood and a shard with customer/legal counsel/third party. I attached the MOU template in our internal runbook (PrivateDeploy_Runbook_v1.2.pdf references it).

3) Operator access: JIT with RBAC and MFA is enforced. All operator keystream calls are recorded and logged to our audit pipeline (retention aligns with SOC2 scope; we can provide a retention table if requested).

4) Attestation language: legal has cleared residency attestation with the caveat 'except as required by law' — we can provide a signed PDF attestation for Clearline.

Attachments referenced: PrivateDeploy_Runbook_v1.2.pdf (internal), HSM_Partitioning_Summary.txt (internal summary).

—Marissa

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency and keystore custody questions for pilot

Alex —

Appended are the artifacts we discussed and the attestation draft. Summary answers below and attachments are linked/included:

- Onshore egress: For EU Private Deploys we operate region-scoped compute and storage. Customer traffic and keystore operations do not egress outside the EU; telemetry that is non-customer-identifiable may be routed to our control plane, which is configured by region policy. See PrivateDeploy_Runbook_v1.2.pdf (section 4.1) and HSM_Partitioning_Summary.txt for details.

- HSM & keystore custody: HSM clusters are logically partitioned per region. We support split-key escrow (MOU template included). Operator access requires JIT approval, MFA, and is fully audited. Logs are retained per SOC2 schedule.

- Attestation: Attached is a draft signed attestation (we can deliver as DocuSign). Link: https://drive.redwood.com/s/clearline/attestation-20260514 and DocuSign: https://docusign.com/xyz/clearline-attestation

Attachments (attached in this thread): Redwood_SOC2_Summary_v1.pdf, CAIQ_slice_Clearline_v2026-05.xlsx, PrivateDeploy_Runbook_v1.2.pdf, HSM_Partitioning_Summary.txt

If you'd like, Marissa can join a 30-minute call Thursday 5/14 11:00 AM CET to walk through the keystore flow and runbook excerpts. Would that work?

Thanks,
Mina
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
